summary: Defines the rsync URI scheme, a way to write a link that names a file or directory reachable through the rsync file synchronization protocol. It is published for information only and is not a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: It is a way to write the address of a folder so that a copying program knows where to go to fetch it.

questions: what is the rsync uri scheme
what is the default rsync port
what is the format of an rsync url
does the rsync uri support ssh
subtitle: The registration of the rsync:// URI scheme, so rsync sources and destinations can be written as links.

tldr.problem: The rsync utility had no registered URI scheme, so there was no standard way to write down an rsync source or destination as a URI.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers the provisional scheme rsync, with the form rsync://[user@]host[:PORT]/Source, built on the generic URI syntax of RFC 3986.
tldr.outcome: It covers rsync over TCP only, with a default port of 873, and adds no special security concerns beyond those of URIs in general.

today: RFC 5781 is an Informational RFC. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: URIs were previously defined in RFC 2396, which was obsoleted by RFC 3986. The procedures for registering new URI schemes are defined in RFC 4395. The rsync utility provides fast incremental file transfer, and this document defines a URI scheme for it.
sections.eli5: People wanted a standard way to write the address of a folder that rsync can copy. This RFC gives that address a proper name.

sections.title: The rsync URI Syntax
sections.content:
The generic form is rsync://[user@]host[:PORT]/Source. An rsync URI describes a source or destination for the rsync application, including a hostname, a path, and an optional user and port. It follows the general syntax of RFC 3986 and is defined in ABNF as "rsync:" hier-part, where hier-part comes from RFC 3986.

The URI may be used as either a source or a destination. If the port is not specified, it defaults to 873. Since only standard elements from RFC 3986 are used, there are no special encoding considerations.
sections.eli5: The address says who to call, which folder to look in, and optionally which door (port) to knock on. If you do not say, it knocks on door 873.

sections.title: Scope and Interoperability
sections.content:
The scheme is for the rsync protocol using TCP as the transport. Other transports, such as rsync over SSH, are not supported by this URI scheme. The registration status is provisional.

The only application that uses rsync URIs is rsync, so the RFC expects few interoperability concerns.
sections.eli5: The address only works for the plain rsync way of talking, not for the version tunneled through SSH.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content: IANA registered the provisional scheme using the template in the RFC. For security, Section 7 of RFC 3986 applies: the considerations about reliability and consistency, malicious construction, rare IP address formats, sensitive information, and semantic attacks all apply, while those about transcoding do not. The scheme has no particularly unique security considerations, and the security of the rsync protocol itself is not covered.
sections.eli5: An rsync address is only a label, so it has the same risks as any web link, such as a tricky-looking address. How safe rsync itself is gets decided elsewhere.
